checks.evidence: Static checks passed: Guard B found no migration sorting before the base branch's newest version 20260911214438; the #1235 expected-count guard, the verify-cost guard (1 added migration, no prohibited verification read) and the #1684 EOL reference guard all passed.

Guard verified green on the tree AND red on seven known-dirty variants: filter removed, role called but result ignored, member role dropped, head source swapped back to public.erp_items_current, transaction-attested head source lost, both non-licensed divisions dropped, and a commented-out filter. A guard never shown to fail is not evidence.

Initially REFUSED with 'migration writes undeclared objects: table plm.item_missing_attribution'. The refusal was correct: granting and revoking on a view registers as a write against 'table <name>' as well as 'view <name>'. Confirmed by running dispatchObjectKeys directly over the migration - removing the grants drops the table key, and spelling them 'on table' does not. Claim #2819 was expanded to declare all three objects rather than stripping the view's permission hardening or weakening the extractor.

assumptions_resolved: Version 20260911230553 is the version reserved by author claim #2819, and the permanent reservation ref was verified present by the lease check.

The issue's core claim was verified before any file was written and is still TRUE: no SQL implements the exclusion. A production scan of every non-system function body, view and materialized view matching prepack|pre_pack|assortment returns only DAM-order objects and api.plm_item_list, none of which filters a missing-attribution population. One issue detail is inaccurate - its pg_proc scan does not return empty, it returns unrelated matches.

The issue's named head source is WRONG rather than stale. public.erp_items_current is a frozen DesignFlow snapshot last synced 2026-05-21; of its 1,454 prepack rows, 1,437 are live prepack MEMBERS and exactly 1 is a live head. The implementation therefore sources from ColdLion and references neither erp_items_current nor api.plm_item_list, both of which open claim #2778 holds.

coldlion.prod_history_component was re-derived rather than assumed: every head-bearing row is self-referencing, so it is a flag meaning 'this ordered item is a prepack head', not a head-to-member explosion. An earlier reading as an explosion would have produced a confident but false 'the head/member labels are inverted' finding, and was discarded.
The re-derivation reproduced unmapped-licensor-population.md's licensed-division figure of 2,016 exactly, an independent validation of that settled document.

Re-scope, recorded for the reviewer: #2611 is framed entirely around heads, but within licensed divisions heads contribute 7 of the 1,770 rows the exclusion removes and members contribute 1,763, because 954 of 961 apparent heads sit in EH001/EP001 which the division rule removes first. Both roles are excluded behind one function and the regression guard covers both.

Two errors in docs/business-rules/product-items-and-identifiers.md that this work disproved were corrected: the head/member table mislabelled erp_items_current.prepack_code as heads, and a paragraph claimed an inventory row's prepack code identifies an assortment head when coldlion.inventory.prepack_code is empty on every production row.

The public-data-venue test failure is pre-existing and outside this contract: it fails identically on untouched origin/main and on other open pull requests, over eight docs/verification/database-efficiency CSVs this lane did not author. It is already owned by issues #2390 and #2391. No evidence file was deleted and no guard was relaxed.

The throughput truth audit refused this branch with 'found 288, recorded 277'. Verified NOT pre-existing: a pristine-main probe passes at 277. All 11 new sites are genuine prose about a missing-attribution population, so each received a hand-written 'excluded' disposition rather than being reworded to dodge the pattern, which would have left the guard green while defeating it. The count and digest were recomputed mechanically from the guard's own discover(), never hand-incremented. origin/main still read 277 immediately before the write, so no rival lane's edit was overwritten.
